There is no longer a cap on companies, but there is one on attention: you can run up to 5 in person; from the 6th on, they all lose reputation every month until you group them.
  • 🛒 Companies for sale (My companies): businesses in your country with real history. Check the figures with an audit before bidding: some hide debts or inflate their sales. You offer 80, 90 or 100 % of the price and the dice decide; you can pay half with credit (it stays as the company's debt).
  • 🏛️ Groups: bring companies together, hire a director (growth, efficiency or conservative) and take advantage of the synergies between companies in the same line of business. Sweep spare cash into your money or move it to the company that needs it.
  • 🏢 Stock market control: on the page of a company on the Stock exchange, launch a tender offer for 51 % with a premium of 20, 30 or 40 %. With control you choose its strategy and its director; dividends reach your money.
Buying a company that already works saves the start-up phase, but the buyer knows less than the seller (asymmetric information): that is why audits exist and why the price is negotiated.

Every 6 months, businesses in your country appear with 12 months of real history. The figures may be dressed up and some hide debts: the audit reveals them. You offer 80, 90 or 100 % of the price with a visible probability; a seller in a hurry raises it. With credit you pay half and the other half stays as the company's debt.
Conglomerates bring companies under common management: they save costs and share customers (synergies), but a bad director hurts them all at once.

You can run up to 5 companies in person; from the 6th on, they all lose reputation every month. Not in a group with a director: they earn a salary (paid by the companies) and, depending on their style, open branches, cut costs or pay down debt. Companies in the same line of business add synergies.
Whoever holds more than half of the voting shares appoints the board and decides the strategy. To get it, a public offer is made at a premium over the price.

With 51 % you choose the strategy (grow, efficiency or dividends) and the director. Growing raises profits and lowers dividends; dividends does the opposite. If you drop below 50 %, you lose control. Only one tender offer attempt per company per year.
